periph_vtech_guitar.name: VTech KidiStar Guitar I/O Expander
periph_vtech_guitar.description: Reads the VTech KidiStar guitar's I/O expander, so it can be converted into a Santroller controller.
details: Reads its 8 button inputs
Drives the guitar's 8 LEDs (on / off)

periph_secondary_pico.name: Secondary Pi Pico (I2C Coprocessor)
periph_secondary_pico.description: Put a second Pico in the guitar neck to read the frets and sensors there, and send them to the main Pico over I2C.
details: The second Pico runs Santroller in peripheral mode, and the main Pico keeps it updated over I2C
Only 4 wires between body and neck (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL)
Can read buttons, analog inputs and devices like matrices in the neck

exp_mpr121.name: MPR121 Capacitive Touch & Slider Sensor
exp_mpr121.description: 12-channel capacitive touch sensor. The best way to rewire a Guitar Hero World Tour touch slider.
details: 12 touch channels with automatic calibration
Fixed address (0x5A), so one MPR121 per I2C bus
Wire the World Tour slider to channels 0-4 and the frets to the next channels
Electrodes 4-11 can also be used as digital inputs or LED outputs

exp_multiplexer.name: Analog / Digital Multiplexers (CD4051 & CD4067)
exp_multiplexer.interfaceType: GPIO select pins (S0-S3) + one ADC signal pin
exp_multiplexer.description: Turn one analog (ADC) pin into 8 or 16 inputs with a CD74HC4051 (8 channels) or CD74HC4067 (16 channels).
details: CD4051: 8 channels, 3 address pins (S0-S2) and 1 signal pin
CD4067: 16 channels, 4 address pins (S0-S3) and 1 signal pin
Works for analog inputs and buttons (buttons need external pull resistors)
Optional settle delay for slower CD4051 parts

exp_matrix_switch_network.name: Key Matrix & Switch Networks
exp_matrix_switch_network.description: Read lots of buttons with only a few pins, using a diode matrix or a switch network.
details: Any GPIOs as rows / columns; use diodes to prevent ghosting
Switch networks, where each button joins two pins (like toy guitar or keypad membranes), scanned pin against pin
Useful for arcade panels, dance pads and keyboards

exp_ads1115.name: ADS1115 16-Bit Precision ADC
exp_ads1115.description: 16-bit ADC for whammy, analog sticks or piezos when you need more resolution than the Pico's built-in ADC.
details: 4 single-ended channels
Uses the ALERT / RDY pin (required) to know when each conversion is ready
Address (0x48-0x4B) is detected automatically
Less noise and more resolution than the Pico's 12-bit ADC

exp_rotary_encoder.name: Hardware Quadrature Rotary Encoders
exp_rotary_encoder.description: Optical and mechanical rotary encoders, for DJ Hero platters, dials and spinners.
details: Read with PIO so ticks aren't missed at high speed
Reports movement or position, with adjustable divisor and update rate

led_addressable_rgb.name: Addressable RGB LEDs (WS2812B / Neopixels)
led_addressable_rgb.description: Addressable LED strips and individual LEDs, driven by PIO.
details: WS2812B, SK6812 (RGBW) and WS2813
Frets light up in their note colour when pressed
Lighting for strums, plus Star Power / Overdrive from games that send it (e.g. YARG, Stage Kit)
Player number LEDs, plus rainbow and fade animations

led_apa102.name: APA102 / DotStar High-Speed SPI LEDs
led_apa102.description: Addressable LEDs with a separate clock line, so they don't have the timing issues of single-wire LEDs.
details: Hardware SPI at 12 MHz
Separate data (MOSI) and clock (SCK) lines
Any colour order (RGB, GRB, BGR, etc.)

led_stp16cpc.name: STP16CPC26 Constant-Current LED Driver
led_stp16cpc.description: 16-channel constant-current LED driver, for original guitar LEDs, button backlights or arcade buttons.
details: 16 outputs per chip, chainable for more, with one resistor setting the current for all of them
Controlled over SPI (MOSI, SCK, LE, OE)
No resistor needed per LED, which suits custom PCBs and lit frets

led_dmx512.name: DMX512 Stage Lighting Interface
led_dmx512.description: Drive DMX stage lights, strobes and smoke machines in time with the game.
details: Outputs DMX512 (250 kbps) on one GPIO; needs an RS-485 transceiver such as a MAX485
Up to 512 channels; channels can follow inputs, notes, multiplier, Star Power and Rock Band Stage Kit fog / strobe / lights

led_discrete.name: Discrete Single-Colour LEDs
led_discrete.description: Ordinary single-colour LEDs, such as the original faceplate LEDs or player lights, each with a resistor.
details: Player 1-4 lights
Star Power / Overdrive indicator
Status LEDs (Bluetooth connected, console authenticated, console mode)

pwr_max1704x.name: MAX1704x (MAX17043 / 44 / 48 / 49) Fuel Gauge IC
pwr_max1704x.description: Battery fuel gauge for LiPo / Li-ion cells, giving an accurate charge percentage.
details: Reports battery percentage over I2C
Battery level is reported to PS4, Switch, PC (HID) and Bluetooth hosts

pwr_adc_battery.name: ADC Voltage Divider Battery Monitor
pwr_adc_battery.interfaceType: Analog pin (GP26-GP29; GP29 reads VSYS on a Pico)
pwr_adc_battery.description: Measure a single-cell LiPo using the Pico's built-in 3:1 voltage divider.
details: GP29 reads VSYS (about 3.3V empty to 4.2V full)
Divider ratio and voltage thresholds can be set in the Configurator
Reports the battery level to PS4, Switch, PC (HID) and Bluetooth hosts, with no extra parts needed on a Pico

pwr_management_sleep.name: Power Management & Inactivity Sleep
pwr_management_sleep.description: Turn off LEDs and other hardware when the controller isn't being used.
details: Heartbeat pin to stop power banks from turning off
Inactivity pin can hold a MOSFET off or pulse a battery module's power button
Sleeps when idle and not connected over USB, and wakes from a chosen wake button
LED and Bluetooth auto-off timeouts

bus_wii_extension.name: Wii Extension Bus (I2C Input)
bus_wii_extension.description: Read Wii Guitar Hero guitars and drums, DJ Hero turntables, Taiko drums, Classic Controllers, Nunchuks and uDraw / Drawsome tablets through the Wii extension connector.
details: Plug the controller in as-is, no need to open it up
Frets, strum, whammy, joystick and touch slider
Makes a USB adapter for Wii instruments

bus_wii_emulation.name: Wii Extension Port Emulation (Hardware Bus)
bus_wii_emulation.description: Act as a Wii extension (Classic Controller, Guitar Hero guitar or drums, DJ Hero turntable, or Taiko drum) so you can plug into a real Wii Remote.
details: Santroller handles the encrypted extension protocol
Plug into a Wii Remote to play Wii Guitar Hero wirelessly

bus_ps2_controller.name: PlayStation 1 & 2 Controller Bus (SPI Input)
bus_ps2_controller.description: Read PS1 / PS2 controllers (digital, DualShock, DualShock 2, NegCon, JogCon, GunCon, flight stick, mouse) and Guitar Hero, Pop'n Music, GuitarFreaks, DrumMania and Taiko (TaTaCon) controllers.
details: PS2 Guitar Hero guitars, DualShock 2 controllers, Pop'n Music, GuitarFreaks and DrumMania controllers
Pressure-sensitive buttons and analog sticks
Rumble is passed through to DualShock controllers
Makes a USB adapter for PS2 instruments

bus_ps2_emulation.name: PlayStation 1 & 2 Port Emulation (Output)
bus_ps2_emulation.interfaceType: SPI pins (CMD, ATT, ACK, DATA, CLK)
bus_ps2_emulation.description: Act as a PS1 / PS2 controller so you can plug into a real PlayStation or PS2.
details: Can act as a DualShock / DualShock 2 (with pressure buttons), Guitar Hero guitar, Taiko drum, Pop'n Music, beatmania IIDX, GuitarFreaks or DrumMania controller
Plugs straight into the console's controller port

bus_snes_pad.name: Super Nintendo (SNES) / NES Controller Bus
bus_snes_pad.description: Read SNES and NES controllers and the SNES Mouse.
details: Standard 4021 shift register controllers over clock, latch and data
Read in under a millisecond

bus_snes_emulation.name: SNES / NES Port Emulation (Output)
bus_snes_emulation.description: Act as a SNES or NES controller so you can plug into a real console.
details: Plugs straight into the console's controller port
Clock, latch and data handled with PIO

bus_joybus.name: Nintendo Joybus (N64 & GameCube Controller Bus)
details: Joybus protocol handled with PIO
GameCube controllers (including WaveBird) and N64 controllers, with rumble

bus_joybus_emulation.name: GameCube / N64 Joybus Port Emulation (Output)
bus_joybus_emulation.description: Act as a GameCube or N64 controller, for GameCube and N64 consoles and the Wii's GameCube ports.
details: Works with GameCube, N64, the Wii's GameCube ports, and GameCube USB adapters
Console rumble is passed back
Joybus timing handled with PIO

bus_xbox360_rf.name: Xbox 360 RF Wireless Module (Front Panel)
bus_xbox360_rf.description: Wire up the front-panel RF board from an Xbox 360 and connect its USB lines to the USB Host port to make a wireless receiver.
details: Works with RF boards from both original and Slim consoles
Wireless controllers, guitars and drums
Sync from a button or from the Configurator; Ring of Light boot animation

bus_midi.name: MIDI 5-Pin DIN & USB-MIDI Devices
bus_midi.description: Connect electronic drum kits, MIDI keyboards or other MIDI devices.
details: 5-pin DIN MIDI IN using an optocoupler on a UART (31,250 baud)
USB MIDI devices on the USB Host port
Bluetooth LE MIDI (Pico W or Bluetooth dongle)
Note, CC and pitch bend inputs, including Rock Band Pro Guitar MIDI
Map MIDI notes and velocity to Rock Band Pro Drums pads and cymbals

ps3.notes: Works out of the box. The PS3 doesn't authenticate controllers.

ps2_usb.recommendedMode: Rock Band Guitar / Drums or GH Guitar
ps2_usb.notes: These later PS2 rhythm games support USB instruments directly.

ghGuitar.title: Guitar Hero Guitar
ghGuitar.description: Acts like a Guitar Hero guitar on PS3, Xbox 360, Wii and PS2: five frets, strum up/down, whammy, tilt and Star Power.

Supports the touch slider on guitars that have one

rbGuitar.description: Acts like a Rock Band Stratocaster: five frets plus five solo frets, the 5-way pickup switch, whammy and tilt for Overdrive.
features: Solo frets register as solo notes in Rock Band
Pickup switch controls the effects in RB2, RB3 and RB4

rbDrums.description: Four pads, kick pedal and optional Pro Drums cymbals, with velocity.
features: Pro Drums cymbals are reported separately to Rock Band 3 and 4
Electronic drum kits work over MIDI IN or USB MIDI
Crosstalk and debounce filtering for piezo pads

djh.title: DJ Hero Turntable
djh.description: Acts like a DJ Hero turntable: platter encoders, the three stream buttons, crossfader, Euphoria button and effects dial.

festival.title: Fortnite Festival
festival.description: Fortnite Festival is set up with a profile rather than a dedicated mode, so you choose the key bindings yourself.
features: Key bindings: Pick the key for every fret, strum direction and menu button.
Presets: Load bindings for Lead Guitar, Pro Guitar, Drums or Pro Drums in one click.
Consoles: A Keyboard profile works on PS4, PS5 and Xbox without authentication.
Overdrive: Turn on 'Select to D-pad Left' in the profile options so Select triggers Overdrive.

gamepad.title: Gamepad & Arcade
gamepad.description: Modes for regular controllers, dance pads and arcade games.
features: BEMANI controllers on PS2: Pop'n Music, beatmania IIDX, GuitarFreaks and DrumMania
Spice2x (as a DanceCon2040 pad) and PD-Loader (Project DIVA) on PC

wiiBluetooth.title: Wii & Wii U: Wii Remote emulation
wiiBluetooth.subtitle: Connects over Bluetooth. No console mods or homebrew needed.
wiiBluetooth.alertBody: Santroller can act as a Wii Remote over Bluetooth, so you can play Guitar Hero, Band Hero and DJ Hero on a stock Wii or Wii U with retail discs.
wiiBluetooth.hardwarePicoW: Raspberry Pi Pico W / Pico 2 W: uses the built-in CYW43439 Bluetooth radio.
wiiBluetooth.hardwarePicoWWarning: Some cheap "Pico W" boards from AliExpress use an ESP8285/ESP8266 chip instead. These don't have Bluetooth and won't work.
wiiBluetooth.hardwareDongle: Regular Pico + Bluetooth dongle: plug a CSR8510 or BCM20702 dongle into the Pico's USB host port.
pairingSteps: Turn on Wii Remote Emulation for your device in the Configurator.
Turn on your instrument and the Wii / Wii U.
Press the SYNC button on the console, then press SYNC on your controller.
The controller connects as a Wii Remote with a guitar or drum extension.

brainslug.title: Wii: Santroller Brainslug
brainslug.subtitle: Lets Guitar Hero, Band Hero and DJ Hero on Wii use wired USB instruments
brainslug.intro: Guitar Hero and DJ Hero on Wii only look for instruments plugged into a Wii Remote. If you're using a wired USB controller without Bluetooth, Santroller Brainslug is a homebrew patch that makes these games read USB instruments instead.
discSteps: Extract sd.zip to the root of your Wii's SD card.
Plug your instrument into one of the Wii's USB ports.
Insert the game disc and open the Homebrew Channel.
Launch Brainslug. The game will boot with USB instrument support.
brainslug.usbLoaderAlertTitle: Load games from USB, not SD
brainslug.usbLoaderAlertBody: The game has to be loaded from a USB drive. Loading it from the SD card stops Brainslug from loading its modules.
usbLoaderSteps: Extract sd.zip to the root of your SD card.
In /bcs/dols/, rename RGHE52.dol to the Title ID of your game (e.g. SXEE52.dol for Guitar Hero 5). Make a copy for each game you want to use.
Select the game and go to Settings → Game Load.
Set Custom Game IOS to 249 (or your cIOS slot).
Save, plug in your instrument and start the game.

pademu.title: PS2: PADEMU in Open PS2 Loader
pademu.subtitle: Use USB instruments in older PS2 games on a modded PS2
pademu.intro: Older PS2 games, including Guitar Hero 1 and 2, only read controllers in the front controller ports and ignore USB. PADEMU, built into Open PS2 Loader, makes USB controllers show up as PS2 controllers.
pademu.note: Note: Santroller switches to PS3 mode when plugged into a PS2. PADEMU sees a PS3 guitar and presents it to the game as a PS2 Guitar Hero controller. PADEMU only works for games launched from OPL, not retail discs.
steps: Plug your Santroller controller into one of the PS2's USB ports.
Plug a normal PS2 controller into port 2, so you can still get around the menus.
Make sure you have a recent build of <extlink>Open PS2 Loader (OPL) <icon /></extlink>.
Start OPL and press Start to open Settings.
Set Settings For Port to 1P and Emulation to On.

orbis.title: PS4: OrbisInstrumentalizer
orbis.subtitle: Removes instrument restrictions on a jailbroken PS4
orbis.cardSubtitle: A GoldHEN plugin for jailbroken PS4s.
orbis.cardBody: Patches Rock Band 4 and Guitar Hero Live to remove the instrument and authentication checks, so any USB guitar or drum kit works without an auth controller plugged into the USB Host port.

wla.title: Xbox One / Series: Wireless Legacy Adapter (WLA)
wla.body: On Xbox One/Series, Santroller can appear as a Rock Band 4 Wireless Legacy Adapter. No physical legacy adapter is needed, and your instruments do not have to be wireless. The "Always emulate the Rock Band 4 Wireless Legacy Adapter on Xbox One/Series" setting is enabled for new configurations and factory resets; existing configurations keep their saved setting. With it enabled, the adapter stays connected and authenticated while you unplug a controller and connect an instrument, including during the gap with nothing attached.
games: Rock Band 4: Multiple supported guitars and drums can share the adapter. Santroller switches to the game's instrument report layout automatically.
Guitar Hero Live: Use a Guitar Hero Live profile. Guitar reports and standard menu navigation work together, with one GHL guitar per emulated adapter.

Gamepad games and dashboard: Santroller's WLA emulation also includes full gamepad support, including sticks and triggers, so you can leave it enabled for games that use a standard gamepad. When the console signals that an instrument game has lost focus, Santroller returns to standard gamepad input.

Fortnite Festival and specific instrument support: Fortnite Festival does not recognize WLA-connected guitars as supported guitar controllers. You can use a Keyboard profile instead, which works on consoles without an authentication controller or auth chip. For guitar-controller support on Xbox One/Series, turn off WLA emulation and use a single Rock Band guitar profile so Santroller identifies itself as a standard guitar instead. Other games that require a particular instrument identity may also need WLA emulation turned off. Using a forced console mode will always skip emulating the WLA, so using a Xbox One profile on windows will still work as intended.
wla.swapTitle: Swap the Donor Controller for a Guitar
swapSteps: Enable "Always emulate the Rock Band 4 Wireless Legacy Adapter on Xbox One/Series" and configure a matching USB Host profile for your guitar, including the correct instrument type.
Connect the donor gamepad to the Pico's USB Host port and plug the Pico into the console. Wait until authentication has completed before unplugging the donor.
Unplug the donor gamepad from the Pico's USB Host port, then plug in the guitar. The same adapter stays connected and keeps its authentication through the empty-port gap.
wla.swapNote: You can also use a USB hub to leave the donor connected alongside the instruments. Authentication lasts for the current console connection: after restarting Santroller or disconnecting it from the console, connect the donor again.
wla.windowsTitle: Forced Xbox One Mode Uses the Native Controller Identity
wla.windowsBody: When Xbox One mode is forced by a profile, it uses the native identity of the first reporting profile instead of WLA, even with the WLA setting enabled. For Fortnite Festival on Windows, force Xbox One mode on a Rock Band guitar profile so the game sees a standard guitar. Combine this with a hold button on startup trigger and then, this lets you hold a button to emulate a festival compatible guitar.

auth.alertBody: The PS4 and PS5 regularly ask controllers to prove they're official, and will disconnect a controller that can't answer after about 8 minutes. The Xbox One and Xbox Series only check authentication when a controller is plugged in, so you can outright unplug an auth controller once authenticated and it still stays authenticated.

builtIn.title: 1. Built in
builtIn.body: Santroller handles Xbox 360 authentication itself. No extra hardware needed.

usbPassthrough.title: 2. USB passthrough
usbPassthrough.body: Plug an official controller, most third-party Xbox One controllers, or an auth dongle into the USB Host port. Santroller passes the console's requests through to it.

harvestedChip.title: 3. Auth chip (I2C)
harvestedChip.body: Take the auth chip off an Xbox One controller board and wire it to the Pico over I2C. This handles Xbox One / Series authentication without anything plugged in.

noAuth.title: 4. Avoid it
noAuth.body:
Some setups don't need authentication at all:
• Fortnite Festival: Keyboard profiles
• Rock Band 4 on PS4/PS5: PS3 instrument mode

auth.hardwareSubtitle: With one of these on the USB Host port, or an auth chip wired over I2C, Santroller answers the console's auth requests automatically:

xbone.hardware: Official or most third-party wired Xbox One / Series controllers, or an Xbox One auth chip (I2C)
xbone.notes: Most third-party Xbox One controllers work over USB Host. Because auth is only checked when a controller is plugged in, you can unplug the auth controller once authenticated. You can also wire an auth chip from an Xbox One controller to the Pico's I2C pins so nothing needs to be plugged in.

ps4.hardware: DualShock 4 or Mayflash MAGPS4 / MagicBoots PS4 dongle
ps4.notes: Leave the dongle or controller plugged in while you play.

ps5.notes: Needed for PS5 games. MagicBoots PS4/PS5 don't work with PS5 games.

festival.alertBody: There's no dedicated Fortnite Festival mode. Instead you create a profile, which lets you choose your own key bindings, pick keyboard or controller output, and play on consoles without an auth dongle.

keyboard.title: Keyboard profiles on consoles
keyboard.subtitle: No auth dongle needed
keyboard.body1: PS4, PS5, Xbox One and Xbox Series consoles require controllers to authenticate (with PS4 and PS5 disconnecting controllers after about 8 minutes if they can't answer).
keyboard.body2: Keyboards don't need to authenticate, and Fortnite Festival supports keyboard controls. If you set up a Keyboard profile, your guitar or drums show up as a USB keyboard and you can play without any extra hardware.
keyboard.badge: Works on PS4, PS5, Xbox One & Series

pc.title: Playing on PC
pc.subtitle: Controller or keyboard
pc.body: On PC, Fortnite Festival works with both guitar controllers and keyboards:
options: Xbox One guitar mode on Windows: Use a Rock Band guitar profile in Xbox One mode for a standard guitar identity. Santroller does not emulate WLA when Windows is detected, even if WLA is enabled for consoles.
Guitar: Use a Guitar Hero or Rock Band profile with XInput. Turn on Send Select as D-pad Left in the profile options so Overdrive works.
Keyboard: Use a Keyboard profile if you'd rather bind your own keys.

steps.title: Setting up a Fortnite Festival profile
steps.addProfile: Add a profile: Under Profiles in the sidebar, click Add profile and give it a name like Fortnite Keyboard.
steps.setEmulation: Switch it to keyboard: In the profile options, set Device to Emulate to Keyboard / Mouse.
steps.loadPreset: Load a preset (optional): Under Mappings, pick one of the Presets:
presets: Fortnite Festival - Guitar (Lead): frets on D, F, J, K, L and Overdrive on Space.
Fortnite Festival - Pro Guitar: frets on 1-5, strum on Right Shift / Right Ctrl, whammy on Slash and tilt on PageDown.
Fortnite Festival - Drums / Pro Drums: pads and cymbals on the default drum keys.
steps.customize: Change bindings: Click any input to bind it to a different key. Just make sure it matches your Fortnite settings.
steps.navigation: Menu navigation: Bind keys like the arrow keys, Enter and Escape to buttons or button combos (e.g. Start + Select) so you can get around Fortnite's menus.
steps.assignments: Choose when it's used: Under Assignments, set the profile as the default, or have it activate when you hold a button (like Green or Start) while plugging in.

legacyImport.peripheralFirmware: Inputs on the secondary Pico were imported, but it needs to be flashed with the new peripheral firmware.
legacyImport.macroAnalog: A macro (two inputs at once) used an analog input, which the new shortcut input only reads digitally.
legacyImport.peripheralMoved: {{device}} on the secondary Pico was imported onto the main Pico, so check its pins.
legacyImport.inputTypeUnsupported: Inputs of type {{type}} can't be imported yet, so they were skipped.
legacyImport.gh5SliderSkipped: GH5 slider bindings were skipped; set the slider up again with the GH5 neck.
legacyImport.pickupSkipped: A pickup selector binding was skipped; only Rock Band guitars have one.
legacyImport.drumBindingSkipped: A drum binding that the emulated drum kit doesn't have was skipped.
legacyImport.xbox360WakeupSkipped: The Xbox 360 wakeup binding was skipped.
legacyImport.bindingTypeUnsupported: Bindings of type {{type}} can't be imported yet, so they were skipped.
legacyImport.fortniteFestival: Fortnite Festival mode was imported as the controller type it was set up with.
legacyImport.tooManyCombinations: There were too many controllers to try every combination of, so all of them have to be connected for the profile to match.
legacyImport.hostBindingSkipped: A USB host or Bluetooth binding that the new firmware can't read was skipped.
legacyImport.hostDrumPadsSkipped: Drum pad bindings from a USB host or Bluetooth drum kit were skipped; set them up again.
legacyImport.hostSliderSkipped: A USB host GH5 slider binding was skipped; the new firmware reads the slider as the tap frets.
legacyImport.usbHostControllerType: USB host bindings were imported for a {{controller}} controller; add another USB host slot for other controllers.
legacyImport.bluetoothPairAgain: The Bluetooth controller couldn't be imported; pair it again.
legacyImport.bluetoothKeyboardMouseSkipped: Bluetooth keyboard and mouse bindings were skipped.
legacyImport.usbHostKeySkipped: A USB host keyboard binding for a key the new firmware can't read was skipped.
legacyImport.proGuitarFretsCalibration: USB host pro guitar fret bindings were imported with the default calibration.
legacyImport.midiChannel: MIDI bindings now only listen to MIDI channel {{channel}}; change the MIDI slot's channel if your MIDI device uses another one.
legacyImport.pitchBendCalibration: Pitch bend bindings were given the default calibration, so check them.
legacyImport.absoluteMouse: Mouse movement was set to absolute; the new firmware only moves the mouse relatively.
legacyImport.keyboardRollover: The new firmware sends at most 10 keyboard keys at once.
legacyImport.keyboardKeySkipped: A keyboard binding for a key the new firmware can't send was skipped.
legacyImport.turntableSmoothing: Turntable smoothing was skipped; the new firmware doesn't smooth the platters.
legacyImport.combinedOutsideDevice: A combined input outside of its device was skipped.
legacyImport.tapBarSkipped: A tap bar binding was skipped; the tap bar can now only be bound as tap frets.
legacyImport.worldTourSkipped: The World Tour tap bar was skipped; the new firmware doesn't support it.
legacyImport.sliderNoSlider: A tap bar slider binding was skipped; the emulated controller has no slider.
legacyImport.peripheralLedsSkipped: LEDs on the secondary Pico were skipped; they aren't supported yet.
legacyImport.analogLedsSkipped: LEDs on analog inputs used as buttons were skipped, as the new LEDs would fade instead of switching on and off.
legacyImport.peripheralOutputsSkipped: Outputs on the secondary Pico were skipped; they aren't supported yet.
legacyImport.ps2OnPs3Unsupported: PS2 on PS3 mode isn't supported anymore, so bindings and LEDs for it were skipped.
legacyImport.fortniteModesUnsupported: S1 handled Fortnite Festival using modes, while S2 handles it using profiles. The keyboard mode and gameplay toggle were imported as a keyboard profile, but the iOS mode can't easily be imported, so you will need to set that up yourself.

lowPass.label: Low pass
lowPass.description: Smooths out noise faster than the cutoff. Lower cutoffs are smoother, but react more slowly.

responsive.label: Responsive smoothing
responsive.description: Smooths small movements heavily while letting large ones through straight away, like ResponsiveAnalogRead.

snap.label: Snap
snap.description: How quickly it catches up to larger movements (0 - 1). Lower is smoother.

threshold.label: Activity threshold
threshold.description: Stops moving while the input only changes by this much, in 10-bit steps (64 raw units each). 0 never stops.

highPass.label: High pass
highPass.description: Removes slow drift slower than the cutoff, so only movement comes through. The axis settles back to its rest point when held still.

zpd.label: Zero point drift compensation
zpd.description: While the input is near its rest point, slowly follow it, so a hall effect sensor that drifts stays centred.
zpd.window: Window (raw units around the rest point)

rapidTrigger.label: Rapid trigger
rapidTrigger.description: Press and release on movement instead of at a fixed point, for hall effect buttons. Calibrate min as released and max as fully pressed.

actuation.label: Actuation point
actuation.description: How far the button has to be pressed (of its calibrated travel) before rapid trigger starts.

down.label: Press sensitivity
down.description: How far it has to move back down after releasing to press again.

up.label: Release sensitivity
up.description: How far it has to move back up after pressing to release.

continuous.label: Continuous
continuous.description: Keep rapid trigger going until the button is fully released, instead of stopping once it goes back above the actuation point.
